question: Does the identity-proved current-main trace contain a policy-sensitive, viable and functionally separated capacity substrate for one Dusk-only focused-to-sweep sequence: a single-enemy Attack followed later in the same player turn by an all-enemy Attack in a multi-enemy fight?
hypothesis: Focused-to-sweep order is a middle-granularity targeting-topology decision: narrower than the closed generic Attack/Skill cadence, broader than the closed exact named-card pairs, and separable from simply acquiring an all-enemy Attack.

closedFamilyExclusions.namedCardSequencing: Do not reopen Scoreline, Afterimage, their order controls or their commitment fallbacks.
closedFamilyExclusions.genericCadence: Do not subset, shorten, reverse, retune or recarrier the closed alternating Attack/Skill three-card cadence.
closedFamilyExclusions.enemyStatus: Do not use Cracked, Dimmed, Weak, Smolder or another existing status lattice as producer, mediator, consumer or payoff evidence.
closedFamilyExclusions.multiEnemyShatter: The closed multi-enemy-card-Shatter unit is one card producing multiple Shatter events across targets. Fanout instead tests an ordered two-card target-scope sequence, reads no Facet or Shatter event and proposes no Shatter payoff; multi-enemy formation is context only.
closedFamilyExclusions.otherClosedFamilies: Do not reconstruct Kindle, Ward, Shatter, Ember-reserve damage, relic, one-bit setup, action-economy, weak-mend, same-instance repeat, acquisition scalar or private-debt paths.
closedFamilyExclusions.method: No ML, RL, optimiser, policy remap, grammar expansion or adaptive candidate tuning is permitted.

mechanismContract.researchIdentity: dusk-fanout; a research identity, not shipping copy.
mechanismContract.producer: After an exact Duskblade Attack whose authored target scope is enemy resolves while combat remains live, set one non-stacking turn-local focused mark.
mechanismContract.mediatorState: One player-combat Boolean focused mark plus one paid flag for the current player turn; neither is a RunState or save field.
mechanismContract.consumer: A later exact Attack in the same player turn whose authored target scope is allEnemies consumes the focused mark after its unchanged authored effects, only in a fight that began with at least two enemies and while combat remains live.
mechanismContract.payoffOperation: After consumption, request exactly one Ember through the existing bounded Ember operation, at most once in that player turn; requested and realised values remain separate telemetry.
mechanismContract.lifecycle: The focused mark and paid flag clear at each player-turn start and combat end. Repeated focused Attacks replace the same Boolean; a sweep before any focus does not prime or pay.
mechanismContract.naturalCost: Acquire an existing all-enemy Attack, draw and pay for both cards, enter a multi-enemy fight, and deliberately play a single-enemy Attack before the sweep in one turn.
mechanismContract.acquisition: None. Existing current-main reward pools, rarities, cards and deck/save representation remain unchanged.
mechanismContract.duskBoundary: The existing Emberheart is the proposed Dusk gate. Ashwarden and mechanism-off are exact current-main paths; Emberheart's authored post-combat healing is unchanged.
mechanismContract.factorIsolation: Scoreline and Afterimage are fixed off and absent. Fanout reads only card type, authored target scope, initial enemy count, current turn and exact Emberheart identity.
mechanismContract.rngAndPersistence: No RNG call or cursor movement, no new run-persistent field, internal ID, save version, content entry, reward entry or acquisition UI.
mechanismContract.telemetry: Direct research-only producer, mediator-set/replacement, consumer, mediator-consume, payoff and turn-expiry stages with card ID, target scope, requested Ember and realised Ember.

fanoutPayoff.definition: Dusk-only focused-to-sweep turn-local mediator and one-Ember payoff defined by the complete mechanism contract.
fanoutPayoff.status: Only a natural opportunity proxy is evaluated here. The non-null level may be implemented only after capacity success.

scorelinePayoff.status: Fixed absent; used only as an immutable overlap anchor.

afterimagePayoff.status: Fixed absent; used only as an immutable overlap anchor.

frozenCausalFactors.independence: Only fanoutPayoff could vary in a later experiment. No acquisition, payoff-value, direction, carrier, status or cross-package factor is opened here.

current-main-trace.meaning: Identity-proved explicit-null current-main observations. Deterministic code reconstructs only the non-interventional upper-bound opportunity.

design.type: zero-new-row complete-cohort capacity and alias audit; not a factorial and not a causal experiment
design.construction: Evaluate the one frozen focused-to-sweep predicate over every player turn in every multi-enemy fight in all 256 rows, then apply exact support, reverse-order, sweep-exposure, breadth, viability, reliability and package-separation rules.
design.cardScopeRule: The producer is an Attack with authored target=enemy. The consumer is a later Attack with authored target=allEnemies. Skills, Powers, statuses, Art, potions, damage events, Shatter events and target indices are outside the grammar.
design.fightRule: Only fights whose frozen starting formation contains at least two enemies are eligible. At most the first qualifying pair per player turn is counted, matching the proposed once-per-turn payoff.
mechanisticallyJustifiedInteractions: Focused Attack by later sweep is structural legality: neither isolated card scope is a candidate mechanism.
Multi-enemy starting formation by ordered pair is a deterministic eligibility boundary, not an estimated product interaction.
Aspect by fanout is a deterministic Dusk/Emberheart boundary reserved for identity; no Ash endpoint is estimated here.
design.aliasStructure: Exact producer-consumer card IDs are breadth witnesses, never candidate cells. Sweep-before-focus is the sole frozen reverse-order witness, not a second candidate. Any-sweep exposure is a one-sided alias control: fanout must leave robust sweep-owning/playing policies inactive, proving acquisition alone is insufficient. The one-card cross-target Shatter family has no shared event unit or payoff.
design.interference: No Scoreline or Afterimage setting varies. Their current-main opportunity sets are shared anchors used only to reject repertoire aliasing. No joint package cell has decision value before fanout identity and capacity pass.
design.omittedCells: No reverse-direction candidate, adjacency variant, same-target variant, status, Shatter, Facet, damage, Ward, Energy, acquisition, reward, payoff sweep, policy control, Ash intervention, RandomBuild, simulator, held-out, joint-package, ML, RL, optimiser or protected-seed cell is authorised.

sourceAnchors.meaning: Complete current-main Attack/target=allEnemies content inventory. Observed breadth may be smaller but must cross its preregistered minimum.

trace.selectionRule: Read the complete sole 256-row co-hand-telemetry explicit-null arm. No row, policy, seed, fight, turn, card, pair or endpoint is selected after observation.

cohort.identity: Every policy and seed from the complete identity-proved current-main rectangle is used exactly once; there is one frozen policy snapshot per identity across its four seeds.

scoreline.definition: A robust policy plays Chisel before a later Executioner in one fight in at least two of four frozen rows.
scoreline.status: Immutable overlap anchor only; the Scoreline family remains closed.

afterimage.definition: A robust policy simultaneously holds Ward and Warden's Edge in at least two of four frozen rows.
afterimage.status: Immutable conservative overlap anchor only; the Afterimage family remains closed.

anchors.reverseOrder: Robust sweep-before-focus policies that are not robust focused-to-sweep policies prove the declared direction is a policy-order decision rather than a symmetric topology label.
anchors.sweepExposure: Robust any-sweep policies that are not robust fanout policies prove acquisition and use of an all-enemy Attack are insufficient for activation.

estimands.unit: Policy identity over its complete four-seed rectangle.
estimands.active: At least one focused-to-sweep opportunity in at least two of four rows.
estimands.inactive: No focused-to-sweep opportunity in any of four rows.
estimands.viable: An active policy with at least one qualifying row that wins.
estimands.reverseOrder: Robust sweep-before-focus policies minus robust focused-to-sweep policies.
estimands.sweepExposure: Robust policies playing any all-enemy Attack in a multi-enemy fight minus robust focused-to-sweep policies.
estimands.breadth: Distinct exact producer cards, consumer cards and ordered exact pairs over all qualifying turns.
estimands.separation: Candidate-only, anchor-only, cross-active and Jaccard policy-set overlap against the separate Scoreline and Afterimage anchors.
estimands.reliability: Pre-existing stall/error rows in the immutable trace; no added-fault estimand exists because no simulator or intervention runs.
estimands.notEstimated: Mechanical identity, actual target/hit eligibility, mediator activation, Ember payoff, causal complementarity, duration effect, Ash isolation, RandomBuild/global-power movement, held-out reproducibility, package admission, detector score, product balance or protected confirmation.

gates.provenance: The 16-policy support/inactivity, eight-policy viability and package-separation minima, 0.55 overlap ceiling and one immutable baseline-fault ceiling reuse the frozen 64-policy structural-capacity scale. Four producers, three of four authored sweeps and eight exact pairs reject an exact-card alias. Eight reverse-only and sweep-exposure-only policies require an independently expressed order decision beyond direction symmetry or acquisition.

decisionRules.success: Every immutable, source, trace, policy-identity, support, viability, breadth, reverse-order, sweep-exposure, package-separation, reliability, budget and zero-ledger check passes at the sole complete look.
decisionRules.successAuthority: Apply boundary 1: freeze only the exact focused-to-sweep-ember-one contract for a separately preregistered exact-null and direct-mediator identity prototype. Do not vary direction, adjacency, payoff, carrier, card scope or acquisition and do not add a simulator row before that identity protocol is frozen.
decisionRules.futility: Any declared capacity, viability, breadth, order, exposure, separation or reliability gate fails on the complete immutable trace.
decisionRules.futilityAuthority: Apply boundary 2: close the exact focused-to-sweep fanout family without reverse-direction, adjacency, card-subset, payoff, carrier, cohort, policy or method rescue and continue with the next evidence-backed minimal structural mechanism inside #421.
decisionRules.inconclusive: An immutable input, trace, schema, policy identity, ledger or wall-time check prevents the complete deterministic decision.
decisionRules.inconclusiveAuthority: Apply boundary 3: record the exact missing gate at the frozen cap; do not repair, rerun, extend, replace the trace or use protected seeds.

order: Verify live task, repository/archive refs, closed-family evidence, source, task capsule, helper, trace and ledger identities.
Reconstruct every player turn in every frozen multi-enemy fight and the one focused-to-sweep opportunity deterministically.
Apply the exact support, viability, breadth, reverse-order, sweep-exposure, separation and reliability gates once.
Verify the ledger is byte-identical and apply exactly one decision boundary.
executionAndStopping.firstLook: The complete 256-row cached rectangle is the sole look. No source descriptor, predicate, direction, threshold, cohort or endpoint may change after execution begins.
executionAndStopping.stagedConstraint: This stage can reject or justify one identity prototype only. It contains no intervention or comparably evaluated enabled endpoint and cannot support a causal or package claim.
executionAndStopping.stopping: One zero-row complete-cohort look. No sequential peeking, option enumeration, reverse rescue, subset selection, threshold relaxation, cohort replacement or endpoint addition.
